questions.explain: Few-shot, or multishot, prompting puts a few worked examples in the prompt so the model copies their format, tone and structure.
questions.subtitle: Few-shot prompting

questions.prompt: How many examples do prompting guides suggest for best few-shot results?
questions.explain: Three to five well-chosen, varied examples usually work best: enough to show the pattern without crowding the prompt.
questions.subtitle: Few-shot prompting

questions.prompt: A prompt with clear instructions but no examples is called what?
questions.explain: Zero-shot means the model gets only instructions, no examples. Add examples and it becomes few-shot.
questions.subtitle: Zero-shot prompting

questions.prompt: What is a system prompt mainly used for?
choices: Setting the model's role and rules
questions.explain: The system prompt sets the role, tone and rules for the whole conversation. Even one sentence of role focuses the model.
questions.subtitle: System prompts

questions.prompt: What is the best first fix for a vague prompt?
questions.explain: Be clear and direct: say exactly what you want, for whom, and in what format. Models can't read your mind.
questions.subtitle: Be clear and direct

questions.prompt: Why wrap documents and instructions in tags like context and instructions?
choices: To make the prompt look neat
To hide text from the model
questions.explain: Tags help the model parse a complex prompt without mixing up instructions, context, examples and inputs.
questions.subtitle: Structure with tags

questions.prompt: In a long prompt, where should big documents usually go?
choices: At the top, above the question
questions.explain: Put long documents first and the question last. Tests showed up to thirty percent better answers on complex, multi-document inputs.
questions.subtitle: Long context

questions.prompt: For long documents, what helps the model focus before answering?
choices: Asking it to quote relevant parts first
questions.explain: Ask the model to pull out the relevant quotes first, then answer. That grounds the answer in the document and skips the noise.
questions.subtitle: Long context

questions.prompt: Context engineering is mainly about what?
choices: Choosing what goes into the context window
questions.explain: Context engineering curates the smallest useful set of tokens the model sees at each step: instructions, tools, data and history.
questions.subtitle: Context engineering

questions.prompt: Why not stuff everything into the context window?
choices: Attention is limited, so quality can drop
questions.explain: Context is a finite resource with diminishing returns. The more you add, the thinner the model's attention budget gets.
questions.subtitle: Attention budget

questions.prompt: What does compaction do for a long-running agent?
choices: Summarises history to free up context
questions.explain: Compaction summarises a conversation that is nearing the context limit, then continues from the summary with the details that matter.
questions.subtitle: Compaction

questions.prompt: With just-in-time context, what does an agent keep instead of full data?
choices: A copy of the whole database
questions.explain: The agent keeps light pointers such as file paths, links or saved queries, and loads the actual data with tools only when it needs it.
questions.subtitle: Just-in-time context

questions.prompt: Retrieval augmented generation adds what to the prompt?
choices: Relevant passages retrieved at query time
questions.explain: RAG searches a knowledge base for passages related to the question and adds them to the prompt, so answers rest on your data.
questions.subtitle: Retrieval

questions.prompt: Why do tool descriptions matter so much for agents?
choices: The model reads them to pick tools
questions.explain: Tool names and descriptions are loaded into the agent's context. Clear, distinct descriptions help it choose and call the right tool.
questions.subtitle: Tool descriptions

choices: Input that overrides the model's instructions
questions.explain: Prompt injection is input, direct or hidden in retrieved content, that changes the model's behaviour against your instructions.
questions.subtitle: Prompt injection

questions.prompt: Which is a good defence against injection hidden in retrieved web pages?
questions.explain: Keep external content clearly separated and labelled as untrusted data, give the model least privilege, and require approval for risky actions.
questions.subtitle: Prompt injection

questions.prompt: How do you know a prompt change actually helped?
choices: Test it on an evaluation set
Ask the model if it improved
questions.explain: Define success criteria, then run the old and new prompts on the same test cases and compare scores.
questions.subtitle: Evaluation

questions.prompt: For consistent, factual answers, how should you set temperature?
questions.explain: Lower temperature makes the model favour its most likely tokens, so answers are more consistent. Higher values add variety.
questions.subtitle: Inference settings
